problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a fleet of cargo aircraft for a critical three-day airlift operation. They need to select a combination of cargo containers to maximize total priority score while staying within the total allowable payload mass.

The available containers are:
* Container A: mass 9 tonnes, priority 247 units
* Container B: mass 41 tonnes, priority 189 units
* Container C: mass 33 tonnes, priority 76 units
* Container D: mass 5 tonnes, priority 245 units
* Container E: mass 26 tonnes, priority 256 units
* Container F: mass 21 tonnes, priority 169 units
* Container G: mass 31 tonnes, priority 82 units
* Container H: mass 19 tonnes, priority 33 units
* Container I: mass 27 tonnes, priority 43 units
* Container J: mass 30 tonnes, priority 100 units
* Container K: mass 5 tonnes, priority 67 units
* Container L: mass 26 tonnes, priority 128 units
* Container M: mass 19 tonnes, priority 64 units
* Container N: mass 28 tonnes, priority 161 units
* Container O: mass 35 tonnes, priority 25 units
* Container P: mass 37 tonnes, priority 35 units
* Container Q: mass 26 tonnes, priority 221 units
* Container R: mass 34 tonnes, priority 198 units
* Container S: mass 15 tonnes, priority 135 units
* Container T: mass 11 tonnes, priority 65 units
* Container U: mass 8 tonnes, priority 284 units
* Container V: mass 39 tonnes, priority 84 units

Furthermore, due to conflicting documentation, exactly one of Container A and Container B must be included in the airlift.

If Container C is selected, it requires special hazardous material handling that reduces the effective total payload capacity by 10 tonnes.
The maximum aggregate payload mass for the operation is 367 tonnes. The coordinator must determine the optimal set of containers to load.
